new_page.title: Milner Langley Homes, New Development and Acreage Guide
new_page.description: Milner, Langley: the south-east pocket of Willoughby by the farmland, where old acreages are becoming new homes. What works, what doesn’t, and the ALR rules.

blocks.text: Draft for Jared’s approval. Written November 10, 2026 from Jared’s Milner notes and the official sources listed on the page. Jared’s verdict is still to come.

Milner is the small pocket on the south-east side of Willoughby, close to the farmland, around the old crossroads of Glover Road and 216 Street in the Township of Langley, between Langley City to the south-west and Fort Langley to the north-east. The crossroads became Milner Station in 1910, when the BC Electric interurban line came through, and the name, which honours Lord Alfred Milner, won a local vote over “Berry’s Station”. The railway gave local farms a way to ship to New Westminster and Vancouver, and by 1925 the village had shops, homes, a church and a school around the station.

A lot of Milner used to be farmland and one-acre-plus parcels, and the Willoughby side is now a new development area, with stores and shops being added slowly and more development, including stores, planned at 72 Avenue and 208 Street. East of Glover Road it is still farm country, with acreages and older rural houses, Trinity Western University’s campus (22500 University Drive) and Milner Valley Cheese, a farm cheesemaker, on Smith Crescent.

There is no Milner area on MLS®, so its listings are filed under the neighbouring Langley sub-areas, the new homes mostly under Willoughby Heights, and the board publishes no Milner price. Ask me for the recent Milner-area sold list before you set a budget: a new townhome and a farm acreage here are very different purchases.

The village had its own school from 1913, on Glover Road, and Langley High School even ran out of it from 1922 to 1924. The buildings later became the Milner Education Centre, which has since closed, so there is no public school in the old village today. On the Willoughby side, the closest public elementary schools include Richard Bulpitt Elementary (20965 77A Avenue) and R.C. Garnett Demonstration Elementary (7096 201 Street). Langley Schools assigns each address to a catchment school, so check the exact address in the district’s school locator. The King’s School, an independent kindergarten to grade 12 school, has a Milner address.

items.t: Highway 1 is about 5 minutes away off-peak, at the 216 Street interchange, which opened in September 2020.
TransLink route 562 runs along Glover Road between Langley Centre and Carvolth Exchange, with a stop at Trinity Western University.

The nearest SkyTrain will be Langley City Centre Station, east of 203 Street and Industrial Avenue, when the Surrey Langley line opens (expected late 2029). Until then the closest station is King George in Surrey.

blocks.text: Rules that come with a Milner acreage

items.t: About three-quarters of the Township is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and ALR status is set parcel by parcel. Check the exact property on the ALC’s ALR map.

On ALR land, the ALC allows one main house of up to 500 m² of floor area, a secondary suite only inside it, and one additional residence (up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 hectares or less) without an application, as long as the Township’s zoning allows it. Subdivision and non-farm uses need ALC approval.

Many rural properties here run on a well and a septic system rather than Township water and sewer. Get the well tested and the septic inspected, and check septic capacity before you plan to add bedrooms or a suite.

faq.q: How much do homes cost in Milner?
faq.a: There is no published Milner figure: Milner is not an MLS® sub-area, so its sales are counted with neighbouring areas. Most homes here are acreages and rural houses, where the land and ALR status set the price, so ask Jared for the recent Milner-area sold list.

faq.q: Is Milner in the Agricultural Land Reserve?
faq.a: Much of the land around Milner is, and about three-quarters of the Township of Langley is in the ALR, but status is set parcel by parcel. Check the specific property on the ALC’s ALR map.

faq.q: Is there a bus in Milner?
faq.a: Yes. TransLink route 562 runs along Glover Road between Langley Centre and Carvolth Exchange, with a stop at Trinity Western University.

faq.q: How far is Milner from Fort Langley?
faq.a: About 8 minutes’ drive off-peak, 6 km north-east along Glover Road.
